title: Ephemeral token mirroring and degraded-fairness mode for regional limiter outages
creator: Ava Mendes
description: Background: We have observed multiple incidents where regional quota/limiter control plane fragments or becomes unavailable for short windows (10s-2m). Existing failover behavior can either be too permissive (unbounded spike) or too strict (hard blocks), causing either SLO breaches for latency/cost or customer-facing 429s. This ticket proposes a middle-ground: an ephemeral token-mirroring fallback combined with a temporary degraded-fairness admission mode. Goals: (1) keep global SLOs (p90 latency, availability) stable during short limiter outages, (2) avoid large cost spikes from unlimited bursts, and (3) preserve approximate fairness across clients while the authoritative limiter is unreachable. Design summary: - Ephemeral token mirroring: when a region's authoritative limiter gRPC control plane is unreachable, nodes enter a short-lived local-mode where every admitted token event is written to an append-only, low-overhead in-memory delta log (mirror). Each mirrored event includes request key, weight, timestamp, and a local sequence id. Mirror retention window defaults to 180s. - Degraded-fairness admission: local admission uses a conservative, stochastic sampling admission policy that enforces per-client limits with a backoff factor derived from historical usage windows. Instead of strict absolute credits, the node enforces soft quotas using probabilistic drops to converge to fairness. - Reconciliation: when control plane reconnects, mirror is pushed to central quota reconciler which reconciles delta consumption and issues corrective actions (soft credits, negative reconciliation tokens) to clients if necessary. The reconciler also emits compensating metrics and triggers billing adjustments only when mirror reconciliation exceeds thresholds. - Safety knobs: maximum local burst cap (configurable, default 2x configured quota), global emergency breaker threshold (if mirror indicates >10x normal rate aggregated across region), and token TTL to prevent long-term drift. - Observability & runbooks: add a dedicated dashboard tile showing mirror rates, local-mode duration, per-client reconciliation deltas, and expected cost delta. Runbook pages for on-call to diagnose and manually disable local-mode. Rationale and trade-offs: - Pros: avoids visible large-scale 429 storms while bounding cost and enabling fair-share behavior during outages. Enables post-hoc reconciliation to keep accounting consistent. - Cons: introduces complexity in reconciliation and subtle edge cases for state convergence. Probabilistic admission can temporarily deviate from exact fairness. Implementation plan: 1) Prototype in canary region (us-west-2) using an opt-in flag. Implement local mirror structure as a ring-buffer with async flush to central reconciler. 2) Add degraded-fairness admission policy module behind feature flag. 3) Build reconciliation service endpoint and reconciliation worker that consumes mirrors, computes deltas, and sends corrective tokens. 4) Add dashboards, SLO alerting (SLOs impacted: regional availability 99.95%, 99.9% global), and runbook. 5) Gradual rollout: canary -> 2 regions -> global with kill-switch. Metrics and acceptance criteria: - During a simulated control-plane outage (inject 30s-3m), error rate (429) should not increase > 0.5% over baseline for affected customers. - Local-mode should bound additional per-customer token issuance such that aggregated regional consumption <= 2.5x normal for outage windows under 3m. - Reconciliation success rate >= 99.5% for entries within 180s window. - No lasting billing discrepancies beyond compensating adjustments for reconciled deltas. API/operational details: - New config: local_mode_enabled (boolean), local_mode_max_multiplier (float), mirror_retention_s (int), reconciliation_endpoint (url). - New logs: mirror.append, mirror.flush, reconcile.success, reconcile.adjustment.{client}. - New dashboard panels: mirror_ingest_rate, mirror_flush_latency, reconciliation_backlog, local_mode_active_by_node. Tests and validation: - Unit tests for ring buffer, mirror serialization, and probabilistic admission. - Load tests: chaosmonkey control-plane disconnect during steady-state traffic and synthetic heavy bursts. - Integration test: end-to-end mirror push and reconcile with synthetic clients and billing reconciliation simulator. Rollout and rollback: - Rollout gated by canary metrics and manual review. - Global kill-switch: disable local_mode_enabled at control plane and auto-revert if reconcile_backlog grows > 10k events for >10min. Related artifacts: design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Ephemeral+Mirror+Design, proto PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6142, reconciler PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8301. Open questions: - Should reconciliation create automatic negative credits or surface to billing queue for manual review? (proposal: auto-negative credits below configured per-customer threshold, else manual) - Should we expose a per-customer toggle so high-trust customers can opt-out of degraded-fairness? - How to handle multi-region canonical ownership for globally replicated customers? Next steps: technical spike to implement ring buffer and local admission sim (1 week), endpoint prototype (2 weeks), and integrate with observability (1 week).
